title: FourCastNet: First High-Resolution (0.25°) Global AI Weather Forecasting Model
whyItMatters: First data-driven global weather model at operational 0.25° resolution, delivering 1-week forecasts 45,000× faster than ECMWF IFS and sparking the Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and GenCast revolution.
summary: Jaideep Pathak, Shashank Subramanian, Peter Harrington, Karthik Kashinath, Anima Anandkumar, and colleagues (NVIDIA, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, and Caltech) introduced FourCastNet in February 2022 (arXiv:2202.11214; subsequently published in Geoscientific Model Development / Earth2Studio). Built on Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators (AFNO) trained on four decades of ERA5 reanalysis, FourCastNet was the first deep-learning model to match operational 0.25° (~25 km) global weather grid resolution—generating a week-long global forecast in under two seconds (~45,000× faster than the physics-based IFS) and enabling thousand-member extreme-event ensembles for hurricanes and atmospheric rivers.
technicalHighlights: First neural weather model to operate at operational 0.25° global latitude-longitude resolution across 20 key atmospheric variables.
Generated 7-day global forecasts in <2 seconds—roughly 45,000× faster and ~12,000× more energy-efficient than ECMWF’s numerical IFS.
Demonstrated sharp tracking of tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers, proving neural operators could scale to global geophysical fluid dynamics.
caveats: FourCastNet 1 trailed ECMWF IFS in medium-range skill beyond ~3–5 days and exhibited gradual autoregressive smoothing—limitations rapidly surpassed by Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and GenCast.

scoreRationale.foundational: Broke the resolution barrier in data-driven global meteorology via Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators on 0.25° ERA5 grids.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly triggered the global AI weather revolution (Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, NeuralGCM, GenCast, Aurora).
scoreRationale.verification: Open-source code and weights verified independently against ERA5 and ECMWF IFS across global forecasting benchmarks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivered a 45,000× runtime speedup over numerical weather prediction, unlocking massive real-time ensembles.
